content:
Facts: Deceased acknowledged debt to granddaughter for construction work on property; defendants argued this debt plus funeral and succession expenses should reduce estate value for calculating reserved portions.
Legal Framework: Art. 556 Civil Code (fictitious reunion); calculation of reserved portions; estate debts; post-mortem expenses.
Interpretative Issues: Which debts must be deducted from estate for calculating reserved portions; whether post-mortem expenses (funeral, succession taxes) reduce estate value for fictitious reunion purposes; how to prove existence of deceased’s debts to third parties.
Legal Principles: For determining reserved portions, only debts contracted by deceased during lifetime are deducted from estate value, not post-mortem management expenses (funeral, inheritance taxes, succession declaration costs). Post-mortem expenses are accounted for only at division time or reimbursed to those who incurred them. Authenticated private agreement whereby deceased acknowledged debt and authorized third party to perform construction work proves both mandate relationship and debt obligation. Completed construction work visible at succession opening, combined with witness testimony, proves debt existed at death. Debt must be deducted from relictum before calculating reserved portions.
